title: Hastings Street

bikeon.heading: Hastings Street
paras: Hastings Street began as a surveyed village of allotments behind the beach in 1879, and the pioneer Walter Hay was its first landowner, buying three blocks in 1882. For decades the only easy way in was by boat from Tewantin, so it stayed a sleepy holiday spot of boarding houses and a few shops. The road bridges of 1929 changed that, and from the 1930s cafes and guesthouses spread along the beachfront. The street was sealed in the 1950s, and surfing put it on the map in the 1960s. Its low-rise character is no accident: in 1990 the council capped building heights at four storeys across the shire, part of a long local push to keep Noosa low-rise. Nobody is sure where the name came from; one theory points to a Gympie goldfields reef named after the ship Warren Hastings.
